title: Call handoff mediator and namespace contract for cross-protocol tool/function interoperability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers and internal apps use two overlapping call models: (a) OpenAI-style 'tools' with name-based discovery + JSON-schema declared params, and (b) legacy 'functions' used by older Redwood SDKs that rely on positional/implicit parameters and different naming conventions. This mismatch causes runtime routing errors, unexpected tool selection, and degraded UX during streaming (partial outputs) when a tool call is in-flight. Goals: 1) Design and implement a lightweight call-handoff mediator that negotiates call contracts at request time, enabling deterministic routing between OpenAI-style tools and legacy functions without changing the customer payloads. 2) Define a canonical namespace contract and a minimal datastore for semantic name aliases and parameter normalization. 3) Add stream-safe translation for in-flight tool responses so we can maintain chunked/streaming behavior across compatibility shims. Constraints: Keep added latency < 8ms p50 in the hot path for common cases; avoid large memory amplification for KV cache; keep the mediator stateless where possible and fall back to an authoritative alias lookup only when necessary.
comments: 2025-01-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after spike showed ambiguous tool name collisions between openai 'translate' and internal 'translator_v1'. Logged two key failure modes: wrong-tool-routing and schema mismatch on partial output streams.

2025-01-14 - Marco Li: Design proposal uploaded to Confluence. Proposed components: (1) call-handoff mediator, (2) semantic namespace table, (3) streaming delta mapper. Asked infra to evaluate latency budget impact.

2025-01-21 - Infra team (Cheng Wong): Benchmark results: simple in-memory alias lookup adds ~2.3ms p50 on a local microbenchmark; networked lookup (Redis) adds ~6-9ms. Recommendation: try hierarchical approach: in-process cache + async refresh from authoritative store.

2025-01-28 - PM (Lina Ortiz): Confirmed backward compatibility is required for Dedicated customers with strict audit requirements. Need an opt-out for automatic alias resolution and an explicit mapping file support for Private deployments.

2025-02-04 - Design review (Priya Rao): UX for error surfacing in streaming mode proposed: attach 'compat_hint' metadata in stream events so clients can surface actionable remediation without breaking existing consumers.

2025-02-12 - Marco Li: Implementation PR opened (WIP) and end-to-end test harness added for streaming translation of chunked tool outputs. See PR in related_links. Marking tests: unit + e2e in CI are green locally; putting behind feature flag 'compat-mediator-beta'.
acceptance_criteria: Mediator negotiates call contracts at request time and routes to correct backend (OpenAI-style tool or legacy function) with deterministic selection in >= 99.9% of synthetic tests.
Canonical namespace table allows registering aliases and parameter normalization rules; resolving an alias in-process should succeed p99 within 5ms.
Streaming delta mapper maintains chunk semantics and appends compat metadata without breaking existing streaming clients (verified by integration tests against the streaming SDK).
Feature behind 'compat-mediator-beta' flag with telemetry that surfaces route decisions and fallback occurrences.
Security review completed and configuration options available for Private/Dedicated deployments to provide static mapping files.
Performance regression guard: end-to-end generation latency does not increase >5% for typical chat requests in the benchmark suite when mediator is enabled with in-process cache.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight mediator runs in the runtime request path. Flow: request -> mediator (in-process alias cache) -> resolve target -> normalize params -> call target runtime -> streaming translation layer rewraps events -> client.

Alias store contract: minimal record = { canonical_name, aliases[], param_schema, normalization_rules_url, trust_level }. For JSON we store as newline-delimited records in authoritative store. Implement in C++ runtime shim + small Go service for management UI.

Cache strategy: LRU in-process cache with async TTL refresh from control-plane Redis; support per-tenant mappings and per-route overrides. Cache miss path must be fast-fail to authoritative mapping to avoid blocking if store unavailable (use 'no-resolve' fallback).

Streaming details: When mediator translates a streaming tool invocation, it must preserve token boundaries and insert a single compat envelope event on first chunk when name normalization was applied. Envelope field: compat_hint:{resolved_from:source_name, mapping_version:v}.

Telemetry: emit 'call_resolution' event with fields [request_id, tenant_id, requested_name, resolved_name, resolution_path, latency_ms, fallback_reason?]. Use existing telemetry pipeline; add sampling at 1% by default, 100% in beta accounts.
Safety: mediator must validate param_schema before forwarding to target and reject mismatches with structured error codes (400.INVALID_TOOL_SCHEMA).
testing_plan: Unit tests for alias resolution, normalization rules parser, and in-process cache eviction behavior.
Integration tests: end-to-end requests comparing direct target invocation vs mediator-resolved invocation for parity in outputs and streaming behavior.
Chaos test: simulate Redis outage and verify no customer-facing failures when using in-process cache; observe telemetry for increased fallback events.
Performance regression tests: run against internal perf harness (benchmarks/chat-low, chat-high) and verify latency budgets.
Compatibility tests: run supported SDKs (python/js/go) against beta feature flag to ensure streaming client continues to accept events with compat_hint.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta feature flag): deploy to staging and 2 internal teams with sampling 100% and public sampling 1%. Monitor call_resolution telemetry and fallback rates.
Phase 2 (opt-in customers): enable via account flag for early customers and Dedicated tenants; provide migration guide and mapping file format.
Phase 3 (gradual default enable): enable for new tenants and high-compatibility workloads if fallback < 0.1% over a week and performance SLAs met.
Rollback: switch off 'compat-mediator-beta' feature flag globally; a 'safety-kill' that prevents alias resolution and returns structured error guiding customer to explicit mapping.
